text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor

text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

text: Do you have any nausea or vomiting, and have you noticed any pain or burning when you urinate? Additionally, is the pain constant or does it come in waves?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history except noted recurrent urinary tract infections. No history of renal dialysis or known genetic diseases. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works in an office setting.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is surprising given your symptoms, as a normal CT scan typically rules out kidney stones and major structural abnormalities. speaker: Doctor
text: The urinalysis shows significant inflammation with WBCs and positive leukocyte esterase, suggesting an infectious process despite the negative nitrites. Given the recurrent UTIs and normal CT, I need to confirm the causative organism. REQUEST TEST: Urine_Culture

speaker: Doctor
text:
A normal urine culture despite significant inflammation on urinalysis and recurrent symptoms is highly suggestive of a non-bacterial cause or a resistant organism. Given the flank pain, hematuria, and sterile pyuria, I am concerned for renal tuberculosis or interstitial nephritis.

REQUEST TEST: Urine_Acid_Fast_Bacilli_Culture

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of sterile pyuria, hematuria, and flank pain with negative bacterial and TB cultures strongly suggests an autoimmune etiology, specifically IgA nephropathy or another form of glomerulonephritis. DIAGNOSIS READY: IgA Nephropathy
